newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's top court clears disputed speaker vote.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's top court clears disputed speaker vote.

text.p: Kuwait's Constitutional Court on Wednesday ruled that a disputed October vote to elect a speaker for the Gulf Arab state's parliament was valid, a judicial source said.
"The ruling means that the election procedures were correct," said the source, who declined to be identified.
Opposition veteran Ahmad al-Saadoun had been declared speaker after getting 30 votes out of a total of 60. His opponent, former finance minister Jassem al-Kharafi, won 29. One ballot was blank.
Kharafi had said that an absolute majority of the present deputies was not achieved, as required by the constitution, and therefore the election should be repeated.
But the court ruled that the deputy whose ballot was blank should be considered absent, meaning that 30 votes were enough for an absolute majority.
